Removed some metal from the mounts, bent them 90 degrees, and both peices of the front fender now bolt horizontally through the Fork hole (where U brakes used to bolt to on the forks). Testing it on my full rigid fat bike, hucking down some dropoffs and over major roots, the fenders now stay perfectly in place.

Now, I'm an engineer and trust me, I know what I'm doing. I tried different settings for sensor sensitivity (only high, mid and low are available). At high setting it keeps taking pictures every second, regardless of any motion in front of the camera. At mid setting, it only takes a picture of I walk in right front of it. Anything past 5-6 ft isn't detected at all. Low setting only works if I put my face right in front of the camera (1-2 ft). Keep in mind that I bought 2 of these cameras (yes I know, should have tried one first). Both work identically and both are totally useless for detecting game or people past 6 feet.
So, I just wasted money on no-name junk products made of Chinesium. Lesson learned.....again. I'm not rich enough to buy cheap things. Buy good, well knows brands! Buy once, cry once!.

text_fidelity_a:
QuiFit 32 oz Motivational Water Bottle - with Time Marker & Straw Lid,Cycling Sport Water Bottle,Non-Toxic BPA Free,Leak-Proof,for Fitness and Outdoor Enthusiasts (Blue) This is a tall water bottle. It stands right at 11.25”. It’s 3” across. I have the blue bottle, and it’s a really nice cobalt blue.

This water bottle has a straw inside. But the straw is removable, if you choose not to use it. But if you indeed use it. . . there are two things to take note of.

#1. A straw brush is not included. Straws like this can get very yucky inside very quickly. The only way to clean them is to use a straw brush, which is not included. If you don’t already have one, you’ll certainly want to make sure to purchase one separately.

#2. There is “bump” right in the middle of the bottom of the bottle. I’m sure this is there due to the manufacturing process. But the end of the straw is just barely above the “bump”, so you’ll probably want to slice-off a little bit of the end of the straw for better flow.

There is no information to show if this water bottle is dishwasher safe or not. But usually with bottles like this. . . even through they are plastic. .. It’s better to hand-wash because at the very least the writing on the outside will probably come off if you place it into the dishwasher. A bottle brush will be needed, and that too will need to be purchased separately, if you don’t already have one.

This water bottle does not have a “locking lid”, per-se. But there is a cap that covers over the mouthpiece when closed. There is a silicone strip around the top to make it easier to unscrew.

A nylon carrying strap is included.

Made in China.

NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates for Women Men Double Row Shiny Indoor Outdoor Skates for Unisex Girls with Shoes Bag [[VIDEOID:6a9dae27c4383bb5bbbf63af76ea0b65]] A year ago my wife was using roller blades, but wanting a pair of roller skates to also enjoy. A year ago, she severely broke her foot and was sidelined for seven months, but limited as she came back. Now she’s able to do more, cleared for roller blading, but she had been wanting those skates... so when I had the chance to grab her this pair, I took it. She had to wait awhile, but now she’s had a chance to get on them... These NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates are decent, what she described as good for beginners and moderate skaters, but she had a few things to mention. First, she has a foot size that can be spot on 9 or 9.5 with a range that could workout between, based on the show and it's cut. In this case, ordering online, she wasn’t able to try them on first. In the end, she feels like the overall fit around the foot is good, but snug. The front of the boot - at the toes - is the tightest. She first tried with thicker socks, but settled for compression socks, which worked much better. Leather can sometimes adjust to a foot, stretching a bit to hug a foot, but in this case, we’re not sure. She says the front at the toes is tough - the leather hard - so she can’t imagine it stretching. In the end, she feels like if you’re spot on a size, you should be okay, but if there is even a slight “off” about a foot size, there could be an issue.

Second, The skates look nice, and overall the materials. - leather - seems good. The materials in the base and wheels seem good. They have wheels that are supposed to light up as they role - they do, but it’s hard to see in the light/daylight. We have not tried them in the dark, and we do see a little sparkle, but overall, you’re not going to be rolling in the dark, so what we are seeing, it’s not overly impressive. There is a little video above, but yea, the “light up” to us is not impressive. Third, She loved roller skating as a child through to young adult and wants to go back to doing it again. She loves loves loves roller blading, but there is something about skating she holds dear... We will say, her being unable to do anything like this in a year has made it hard for her - she felt it hard/big/painful and has to take this slowly getting back to it. She got up, she went, and she really liked it a lot. She felt like it’s coming back and she enjoyed the experience. She feels like these NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates are going to let her get back up and going - with time to develop - and she’s going to be able to enjoy it. But she also feels like these are beginner to moderate level. The ground itself - the surface - is important. The place we took them (parking lot) was rough and uncomfortable for her. She does have an area she loves for blading, but during several months a year (current) we have a massive amount of acorns that fall and she cannot, for safety, blade (or roller skate) in the area. So this parking lot showed her not every surface is going to work with these skates.

Overall, these ARE decent skates. Things to consider: size, type of sock, surface for skating. These will have an affect on the experience. She sets them best for beginner to moderate. And in the end, she does like them and thinks she’ll get a good amount of use out of them.
text_fidelity_b: NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates for Women Men Double Row Shiny Indoor Outdoor Skates for Unisex Girls with Shoes Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Heated Gloves, Rechargeable Heating Gloves, Winter Touchscreen Warm Gloves for Women and Men, Waterproof Touchscreen USB Heating Gloves for Motorcycle Fishing Hiking Cycling Skiing in order for these to work, you will need some kind of battery pack/portable charger (BOUGHT SEPERATELY of course which ISN'T advertised) And you will have to run these annoying wires through whatever coat you are wearing from arm to arm, and deal with having wires throughout your clothes. You would be better off just getting the ones that use regular built in battery packs.

The fit is nice enough I suppose (given that I have tiny hands). I was expecting them to be too big as they were advertised as adult gloves, but they actually fit quite well. So if you have normal adult sized hands, these may be a bit small for you. They only seem to have heat on the outside of the glove, so I don't know how well these will work for their intended use (for keeping my hands warm while biking this winter) But I guess we will see.

They take quite a while before you start feeling heat too, so you may want to put these on about 5 minutes or so before you head out into the cold. I feel bad giving this 2 stars, but I honestly don’t think it’s spectacular for the money (probably a 3-star bike), but the assembly issues knocked it down to 2 stars, along with the poor instructions. I’ll be sure to buy a pre-assembled bike when we need the next size up.

text_fidelity_a: Stamina 1700 Power Tower It's hard to find something to say that hasn't already been said, but this is a solid piece of equipment if you're under 250lbs (the max weight that the 1700 can support). If you're less than 250lbs, then this is an ideal dip and pullup/chinup station. I'm 6'2" and 185lbs and it handles me fine. There is some flex/movement when doing pullups without proper form (erratic, swaying movement) and dips tend to flex the unit even with proper form (slow and controlled movement), but the overal the 1700 is still stable enough. I would suggest using the amount of movement or sway as an indicator of using proper form. If it's moving a lot, you're probably simply swinging yourself through the pulls and chins or dropping yourself down through the dips like a rock with no resistance (ignoring half of the exercise) without keeping yourself stable.

Pactrade Marine 13 1/2" Destroyer SS 304 Steering Wheel 5 Spoke Teak Wood Cap This is a very nice, solid, sturdy Destroyer wheel. I have a 16 ft. center console and when I replaced the steering gear (steering box, cable) I wanted to put a new wheel on the boat too. The old wheel (heavy emphasis on the word "old") was made of some sort of plasticized hard rubber and it was frankly nasty. Years and years of hand oil, motor oil, motor fuel, fish slime and general grunge had accumulated on and eaten up the wheel. It was time to find a new wheel.

It's hard finding the right size Destroyer wheel because I needed a 13 inch wheel and most of them are bigger. A 13 inch wheel is all that will comfortably clear everything else on the console. Many of the wheels I looked at cost around twice as much as this one did.

The wheels spokes are gathered and locked into a central star and a cover made of what looks like teak wood snaps over the top. The description says "bakelite cover" but mine doesn't look like bakelite, nor does the product picture. Mine looks like the one in the picture. My boat, being a center console, has grab rails around the console but I often find myself using the wheel as a grab hold when moving around on the boat. I'm not a small person, so that's likely considerable stress on the wheel itself. It's not a problem, I've been using this wheel for several months and it's as solid as the day I mounted it.

This wheel is rock solid and a perfect finishing touch for my new steering system. I'm very happy with it and never have hand/fish/oil/fuel/grunge on my helm any more!
text_fidelity_b: Pactrade Marine 13 1/2" Destroyer SS 304 Steering Wheel 5 Spoke Teak Wood Cap

text_fidelity_a:
Srixon Q-Star Tour 3 Golf Balls The long story:
A few weeks ago I hit a ball OB and found a Srixon Q-Star Tour that wasn't mine in the area. I dropped it and used it the rest of the round. Very soft feel, distance was good, and it spun the way I expected. I went back to my usual ball, which I like a lot and still like a lot, but every once in a while I'd pull that Srixon out the bag and play a hole of two with it. That soft feel just kept bringing me back to hitting it. Well, I lost it in a pond on a good shot - LOL! - that the wind pushed too far right. So, I decided to buy some on Amazon.

Jump to today and I used one of them on my weekly league round. Well I shot my best score of the season, putted, chipped, drove, everything was better than typical. On top of that, I used the same ball, literally the same one, for all shots on all 18 holes. Something I never seems to accomplish in the past.

Now I understand there are a lot of factors involved. Most of which fall on my shoulders. However, I'm really having a hard time going back to my old ball now. Even though I really like them.

So, bottom line, they may not give you the best round of the season, but they do preform as well as any ball I've played (better today). The price is half the super premium balls. I'd suggest trying them.
text_fidelity_b: Srixon Q-Star Tour 3 Golf Balls

text_fidelity_a:
Atomic Jumpball Deluxe Double Electronic Basketball Shootout Includes Four Mini Basketballs and Inflating Air Pump Even though we have a regulation basketball hoop in our driveway, here in Ohio with our mostly crummy rainy or snowy weather, we only seem to use it a few months out of the year. Just shooting hoops in the drive is a great way to burn off some calories, and our family always enjoys not just the skill of shooting, but also the competition. We've owned other small basketball hoops that are on a stand for inside or hang over a closet door to have fun with during our long winters and rainy falls and springs, but nothing as nice as this Atomic Deluxe Basketball Shootout.

This Atomic Deluxe Basketball Shootout arrived in just it's store box- no extra shipping box- but it arrived perfect. The box is heavy, so you will need a little help lifting it. Once opened, I immediately noticed how solid the tubular frame is and how sturdy the fabric with netting are. This Shootout is built to last, which is a good thing, as the kids and their friends really love playing with it. The four little basketballs are also very sturdy and this even comes with a pump to keep them inflated. Putting this together with the enclosed instructions and tools took a little over an hour. We took our time with the little infrared sensors, as they are the hardest part to figure out when assembling.

This is electronic, so you'll have to set it up near an outlet for the plug. It keeps score electronically and does make some beeping and click noises as it counts. Whoever makes the most baskets in the allotted time wins and it does count accurately. You can also just play without the electronics any way you like. What I love best about this Basketball Shootout is that the 6 year olds love it just as much as the teenagers. They really enjoy the furious shooting against each other with the 4 balls that keep rolling back to them. It's great to have it in the basement, game room or garage for those that have crummy weather like we have here in Ohio. I love the fact that all ages can enjoy this fun and furious basketball shooting no matter what the weather is like outside. Just for the fun and exercise alone, this sturdy Atomic Deluxe Basketball Shootout deserves 5 Stars.
text_fidelity_b: Atomic Jumpball Deluxe Double Electronic Basketball Shootout Includes Four Mini Basketballs and Inflating Air Pump

DYJ Adjustable Right Handed Tactical Molle Modular Belt Holster for Pistol(1000D) (Black) Discounted or free item
is it good or bad?
I'll make the provider/author
either happy or sad..........
and sometimes even mad.

This is a very well-designed and strongly built holster that can hold a wide variety of pistols -- both revolvers and semi automatics. The holster is constructed of a high quality nylon and utilizes heavy-duty accessories and stitching. It is light and breathable and designed to hold many different sized and configured firearms. While I was unable to determine where it was manufactured, the quality of the construction leaves no doubt that it was designed and assembled by experts. This holster comes with a 30 day money back guarantee (or free exchange) and 24 hour customer service.

While you wouldn't typically use this to hold a sub-compact pistol, it will adequately secure a S&W Airweight, Glock 42, Walther P22, and a Kahr CM9. Stepping up, I also found it appropriate for a Springfield XD Mod 2, S&W Model 66 (or 686), and a Glock 23. It will also work with a Ruger Public Defender, a Keltec PMR-30, and the Ruger MK series. I could almost get a S&W .44 mag Backpacker in it but the sights were too high.

The reason that all of these would fit and be adequately secured is because of the triangular interior construction that is stiff enough to flex and still hold pistols of varying dimensions. Another nice feature is that the inside of the holster is composed of a smooth nylon that will not leave marks on your firearms. For the very reasonable sum of $20.00 you will receive a quality holster that is lightweight and can hold a wide variety of pistols. Tough to go wrong with this one!
text_fidelity_b: DYJ Adjustable Right Handed Tactical Molle Modular Belt Holster for Pistol(1000D) (Black)

Epson PULSENSE PS-100 Heart Rate Monitor with Activity Tracking for iOS - Black M/L The Pulsense seems like a pretty cool heart rate monitor in theory, but unfortunately falls a bit short in actual use. It’s easy to put on the wrist, and the M/L size fit me fine. It’s not too obtrusive, and while not sexy, it’s not horrendous looking either.

Setting up the device and syncing it with my iPhone was pretty easy. And it was comfortable enough to wear all day at first. But the lights and vibrations that notify you on your heart rate (what target zone you’re in) got annoying real fast – thankfully they can be deactivated. And I found myself reflexively looking at the unit whenever I wanted to know the time – but there’s no clock on it, doh! I really wish there was a digital readout that could toggle between clock and heart rate.

When it works, I like the Pulsense a lot. But I found a lot of lapses in data collection, specifically with the heart rate. At times, it shows that I was at a resting heart rate, when I know that I was actually very active. Not really sure why this happens, and I haven’t been able to pin point it to any specific activity, location, etc.

While there is a lot of potential with the Pulsense (especially not having to wear a chest strap), I’m not so sure that it’s ready for prime time. I’m excited to see how the next version will be improved.
text_fidelity_b: Epson PULSENSE PS-100 Heart Rate Monitor with Activity Tracking for iOS - Black M/L

text_fidelity_a: OGIO Half Dome Duffel Bag I have a bunch of duffel bags (sometimes I think I collect them); my favorite is a standard Nike bag, but this one is better if you are looking for really high quality stuff; the main black fabric or material is very thick and heavy duty, I think it will last a very long time.  In addition the main zipper is the heaviest zipper I have seen in several years on ANYTHING.  It seems to hold a decent amount of stuff; one thing that lessens the ability to hold stuff is the design (that's probably why it is called half dome, duh); it's kind of rounded on the top (not the usual squarish or rectangular design of most duffel bags I have owned), so you lose a little room on the top side.  It also has a nice little pocket on the side for an ipod or iphone or whatever small electronic device you want to carry on the outside of your bag.  The main shoulder strap is adjustable and fairly comfortable--but it isn't padded and if you are carrying any fairly heavy things, it isn't comfortable to carry about using the shoulder strap.  It also has a nice fairly solid rectangular bottom piece that fits in the bottom of the bag that provides support for the bag.  One thing I thought almost all duffel bags had was more than one decent sized compartment, usually two zippers with their own sections.  This unit only has the one main compartment (and the  other  really small one for electronic stuff  which does have a small zipper (again, really heavy duty).  It's like a heavy duty jacket zipper.  In sum it is a well made piece of merchandise; it will last years even with some abuse.  One final thing, the main reason I bought this is for airplane trips where you take carry on; this will fit in any airline compartment, and it still holds a reasonable amount of stuff (well, for us men)(I know, chauvinist pig), so it works for me for this purpose.

text_fidelity_a:
Saver Pad Set I had an accident on my skateboard yesterday, hit my elbow pretty hard and quit for the day. I was going to wait for this protective gear before I started practicing Ollies or doing anything else risky, but my sore elbow was a good reminder to wait for the proper equipment to use before something like that (or worse) happened again.
This set of knee, elbow and wrist protectors is fairly well-made although light. The only thing I really don't like is the logo. After years in graphic-arts I have decided that I truly dislike high-visibility logos so I remove them by sanding or cutting them off. In the case of this "Triple-eight" with a horrible intersection of 3 eights the best method was flat black enamel paint that seems to have obliterated everything except the raised portions of the embroidery. Otherwise it's all black and low key. (This was my intent when I bought this kit and it worked well. Yay!)
The fit is fairly good for a mass-produced set of items, the big factor and the determination for S-M-L being the hand and wrist-guard, which I ordered Large. It's a little loose, but I have all sorts of foam sheets and leather pieces to custom-fit these important pieces, even to reinforcing the external portions as required. The knee and elbow pads are sort of a one-size-fits-all, but the same rules for modification apply.
Essentially, a very good buy for protection that is far better to have and not need than to really need and not have!
This is important stuff to wear, because a skateboard can become very dangerous suddenly without any warning. This kit, in conjunction with a decent helmet and good shoes (skate shoes) can make the difference in protecting those parts of your body that won't function very well unless they move freely without pain. Try being an artist or musician with a broken wrist. Try driving you car or riding your bike with a bad elbow or knee. It's in your best interest to protect yourself, because nobody else will, and if you still haven't figured it out getting hurt costs $$$!
text_fidelity_b: Saver Pad Set

text_fidelity_a:
United Cutlery Bushmaster Survival Knife I went through and read the good and the bad reviews. Taking all that into account and knowing what I know about knives, which as a retired chef is quite a bit, I decided to take a chance on this one.

First, even after reading the numerous reviews and manufacturer's info, I was astounded by the length of this knife. It is LONG. Not only is this knife long, it's heavy.

Second, as many noted, the knife blade wasn't all that sharp when received. Again, noting my background as a retired chef, taking care of knives and bringing them from the land of the dead to an item with a wonderfully usuable blade isn't all that difficult providing you've the equipment to do so.

I honed the knife using the medium grit on my tri-stone about 10 minutes then moved to the fine grit stone. That put a good edge on it. While watching Firefly (http://www.amazon.com/Firefly-Complete-Blu-ray-Nathan-Fillion/dp/B001EN71CW/ref=sr_1_3?s=movies-tv&ie=UTF8&qid=1363822981&sr=1-3&keywords=firefly), I pulled out the tri-stone again and continued with the medium to fine grit honing getting an even better blade on it.

The scabbard is appropriate for the knife. That, to me, says a lot. There's a lot of knife, there's a lot of scabbard. One other reviewer succinctly defined the contents of the pockets on the scabbard. I needn't do the same. Nor shall I wax about which pieces are good and which aren't. Everybody's entitled to their own opinions about that. That said, I'm keeping "most" of the prepackaged stuff there. I'm sure over the course of a few trips I'll update, tweak and tune what I want, but for the time being, it all stays.

I'm very satisifed with this knife. I know while I'm backpacking, hiking or camping I'll keep it close at hand. My son's got HIS knife, Whetstone Usa Full Tang Stainless Steel Jungle Survival Knife, (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003U7SC6O/ref=oh_details_o06_s00_i01?ie=UTF8&psc=1), I've got mine.

Happy honing.
text_fidelity_b: United Cutlery Bushmaster Survival Knife

I have an adjustable Indian club and needed something to put inside as a weight. I wanted something that would allow me to break the weight down into at least 0.25 pound increments but not so fine that I'd be sweeping up little bits of it every time I cleaned my floors (because, sooner or later, no matter how careful I am, I'm going to drop and scatter some of it). The material also needed to stand up to being thrown around inside the body of the club as I swung .

This stuff is perfect. It's large enough to easily find when I drop it but small enough to weigh out exactly in whatever increment I work. I weighed it out into 0.5 pound increments and put those into sandwich bags to make changing weights more efficient. Then I started a 21-day training program that required 100 swings per day. The bags needed replacing periodically -- which is understandable as that's definitely not what they were designed for -- but the pellets still look new. I should also note that I did not get 8 pounds as advertised; I got just over 8 pounds and 10 ounces.

I had no idea that plastic corn pellets were a thing until I started searching for filler for my club, but I'm very glad I found this. What I have now will keep me going for a while, but when I'm ready to up the weight, I'll definitely buy another box of this.

text_fidelity_a: Kelty Ridgeway 4 Person Elevation Sport Dome Tent I am an avid camper and in my opinion this tent is ok for indoor use only. Bought a year ago as a backup tent and opened but didn't look at closely.  Just used it last week in the Everglades FL.  The first thing I noticed was the fly is very thin material, unlike my 10 yr old Field and Stream.  While carefully inspecting the fly I noticed a small tear, although it was carefully opened .  The winds picked up during our visit and unfortunately I faced the opening into the wind.  It is really noisy.  Drove to the Keys and had a big rainstorm.  Although I was behind a 4 ft fence to help protect from the wind, the floor was soaked after the rain.  I felt if coming through the fly in many areas and the fly does not cover the front well and the rain comes in the screen on the side.  When I zipped the tent the cloth around the zipper stretched and nearly pulled the seam apart.  The poles and stakes are very cheaply made and the zipper does not appear to be very good quality.  After one use  I decided to buy a new, good quality tent.  I would not buy another Kelty based on this.

infray Hand Warmers, Rechargeable 5200mAh Power Bank Electric Hand Heater USB Portable Charger Double-Sided Heating Pocket Hand Warmer, Safe Heat Therapy Pain Relief Winter Gift for Women Men This is a useful hand warmer for those cold days. It is sized to fit in a pocket, and conveniently recharges with a USB outlet.

I've been using my hand warmer while hunting in the cold November rain. It turns on with a long press of the lone button near the top of the unit. There are 3 heat levels: 35, 45, and 55 degrees C. You can cycle through the 3 levels with short pushes of the control button. The unit heats up quickly, and the display switches automatically to show how much battery is left, once its up to temperature.

The battery, unfortunately, doesn't last very long. At full heat (55 degrees) you get about an hour or two. At the lowest setting, the heater will last longer, but it seems like that depends on how cold the air is where you are using it. If its really cold and you have the heater out and exposed to it, your battery will drain pretty quickly. It will last much longer indoors at room temperature. The lesson here is to keep the heater in your pocket when you can, rather than getting it out and holding it as it warms your hands. If you want it to last all day, turn it on when you need to warm up, then shut it off once you've knocked the chill off. If you only need it to last for an hour or two, to get you through a football game or something like that, you can just let it run.

The recharging port accepts a USB-C plug, the latest format. A charging cord comes with the heater, but there's no adapter to plug it into the wall. Most of us likely have an extra block or two around from our phones or other USB devices.

I wish that the heater was waterproof, or at least weather resistant, to be more useful in really crappy weather. The charging port, for example, is open to the weather so I usually keep the heater in a small ziplock bag when I'm using it in the snow or rain. It works OK that way.

If you haven't used up all the juice in the heater's battery, you can use it to recharge your phone or other USB device. That's a potentially useful utility. I haven't used mine that way yet, though.

The pocket-sized heater works best in a central pocket that you can reach with both hands, like the Joey pouch on the front of a pullover hoodie. If you don't have that, you have to either cradle it in both hands, outside your pockets, to warm both hands at once, or switch it from one pocket to another, to warm your hands one at a time. Another potential use is in the foot of your sleeping bag or bed, to warm your feet, but the heat won't last all night.

Electric heaters in general are notorious for demanding lots of energy. This little heater does produce a nice warm glow in your pocket, but it doesn't seem to have resolved the inherent inefficiency of electric heaters.

Please let me know if you found anything in my review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: infray Hand Warmers, Rechargeable 5200mAh Power Bank Electric Hand Heater USB Portable Charger Double-Sided Heating Pocket Hand Warmer, Safe Heat Therapy Pain Relief Winter Gift for Women Men

Turns out (most) of the hardware is already in place and just needs to be aligned and tightened (with the included tools).

I assembled this on my own and most people should be able to do just like I did. One note on assembly though: the main part of this is the bulk of the total weight of the entire bike. It's a bit on the heavy side so if lifting heavy objects is hard or risky for you you should seek out some help.

The pedals went on super quick and easy. They were clearly marked 'L' and 'R' and the instructions made sure there were clear on which way the bolts should be threaded.

I've since put 320 miles on the odometer on this, so, about 14.5 miles a day. I haven't noticed any mechanical problems or glaring defects. I enjoy the fact the the seat is adjustable to some degree and the adjustable tension works surprisingly well.

My reason for giving only four stars is because of the seat. It is very hard and after a while it causes pain. I'm going to get a nice cover for it and hopefully that will help some with that.

Other than that, this is a great bike for the price.

The fact that it still calls for perishable (3 year expiration date) packets is a bit disappointing. I assume so, whether via P&G branded packets or something chemically similar/identical, but it's still a bit of a monkey wrench.

I highly recommend people have a purification solution, and I have no reservations about recommending this, but I'd also consider systems that do not need packets.

text_fidelity_a:
Gun Sight Compatible with Salt&Gun 3.0 2.5 2.0 with Manual and Constant Lighting Modes (Gun not Included) This laser comes with six batteries and you only need three so you have one set for backup. The laser itself in my opinion works good and is bright with a thin beam. You can adjust the beam with the included tool. The attached button cord also works good. I could turn it on and off easily and it always worked properly. Mounting the laser was also a non-issue and tightened good.

The problem with this laser is the button switch located on the back cover of the laser. I had a horrible time getting it to work properly. After studying this thing for awhile, I discovered after removing the battery cover that the spring was crooked and would move the batteries out of position. The result was that the spring tension and spring not making center contact was causing the laser to not work properly. The spring was loose and wobbly too. I tried bending it to center but it only made it worse. My husband had spare various size springs in his shop so was able to remake one that fit better. After about an hour of work we finally got it fixed. My husband put it together in a couple of hours. The only time he needed my help was to assemble the parts that goes under the machine that makes it able to fold.
Once ready it is pretty sturdy. Obviously not as the ones at the gym, but mostly because it is smaller. The “bed” is shorter than the pro, but that’s exactly why it is perfect for a house, in my case for my garage. It is somewhat light weight. You can move it a little.
As soon as you press start it ask you to connect it with IFIT. I did not do that. I pressed the iFit button for 30 seconds and it was override. The machine is very smooth. No weird sound beside the normal sound of the belt running.
This machine does not have a fan (I don’t need it) , and has good speakers.
I do mostly sprints, so I move from power walking with encline for 1 minute to all out for 1 minute for 15-20 min, and the machine works perfectly in those speeds and incline changes. It does change the speed fast. So you need to be attentive.
My 5’’ screen shows me cal, distance, time, laps...
The folding process is super easy! And like I said before it is not super heavy, and when going down to the floor is smooth, soft and slow. It does not fall fast.
It has a space where you can put your phone or tablet on the front. 2 cup (or towels or whatever) holders on the sides. And the STOP button with the strap for emergency.
Since “we” put it together I’ve been using it everyday. And I really like it. I could definitely recommended it.

24BattlePack Tactical Backpack | 1 to 3 Day Assault Pack | Combat Veteran Owned Company |40L Bug Out Bag (Ranger Green) Just finished our first bushcraft day with this pack and loved it. LOVE the included D ring thank you so much I use it for so many things. The rubber flag patch is tasteful. I don’t even want to switch it out for anything. We started a fire in light rain and wind in upstate NY in 42 degrees. It’s not easy!

We packed clothes, binoculars, food and water, knives and a hatchet. First aid kit, hats, safety glasses, phones, chargers and work gloves. And it had plenty room to spare. It didn’t rain hard but my stuff stayed dry.

I like the side buckles and steals to decrease the size and really compress the gear into a smaller package so it moves less while walking. The zippers slide VERY smooth. My lady likes how it opens up full butterfly to pack it like a suit case! I think that’s cool too.

The chest and waist buckles are a must and appreciated on rock scrambles and hills. This is my new bushcraft bag and possible long hike back. (I’ll just throw my 2L water bladder in there). Plus the padding that contacts my back allows some air flow which doesn’t prevent sweat, but reduces back heat which I like.

It may also become my shooting range bag but we will see. But if you need a single or multi day bushcraft bag with a tactical look and feel, it’s solid.
